note: The Gomens of Section II. Lore is [D] design (would, designed to, grown) except the Circle, whose body is people [M]. Readings name the radicals in each Gomen's cartouche, in the script drawn by src/glyphs/script.mjs.

gomens.name: The Clearers
gomens.lore: Folded from the body’s own proteins, a Clearer would drift in the blood like a seedling in a stream, opening its hands to every thread of plastic it meets. What it gathers it carries out; when the work is done it dissolves into nothing the body cannot use.

gomens.name: The Shore-walkers
gomens.reading: the house that eats what the sea returns
gomens.lore: Shells grown from the carbon they eat, faceted like crystal and bright like oil on water; legs that hold the sand the way roots do. A Shore-walker would sort the tide line all day, plastic into the slow furnace under its shell, everything living left where it lay. Hand one a bottle cap and it would chirp.

gomens.name: The Circle
gomens.lore: Grief no one has processed is waste too, and no machine can metabolise it. People do, together. This is the one Gomen whose body is us: a ring of hands around a heart, holding what no one holds alone.

gomens.name: The Weavers
gomens.lore: Under a forest, fungal threads trade water and minerals for the trees’ sugar, and may pass what one tree has to another. Weavers would carry that pattern into supply chains and data: threads that move and never hoard, grown where a link is needed and dissolved when it is not.

gomens.name: The Gleaners
gomens.reading: the leaf that gathers the sky
gomens.lore: A seed pod with leaves for solar wings and a net spun like silk: a satellite grown rather than launched. A Gleaner would drift through low orbit gathering what launches left behind, bind it together, and ease it down to burn away high in the air.

key.lede: Written in a script imagined for the people who would tend them. Every mark descends from the logo (star, bead, figure, tree) or from the painting (vessel, crystal, root, stream).

radicals.bead: a seed, a scale, a count
